intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers stunning views of Lake Harris, the Darran Mountains, and cascading waterfalls. Book a guided day section or multi-day hut experience.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing – South Island Alternative: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Tackle the iconic Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a challenging 10km return hike gaining 1000m elevation. Reward yourself with panoramic views of the Hooker Valley, Aoraki/Mount Cook, and the Southern Alps glaciers. The hut overnight option offers a magical sunrise over New Zealand's highest peak.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with a short rainforest hike along the Milford foreshore track. Paddle beneath towering Mitre Peak, spot fur seals and dolphins, and witness thundering waterfalls up close. This immersive full-day experience connects you with Fiordland's raw wilderness from both land and water.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening food walk through the town centre and waterfront. Sample locally sourced Central Otago pinot noir, South Island lamb sliders, Bluff oysters, and artisan cheeses at five curated stops. Learn about New Zealand's food culture and farm-to-table philosophy from passionate local guides.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing – South Island Alternative: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Tackle the iconic Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a challenging 10km return hike gaining 1000m elevation. Reward yourself with panoramic views of the Hooker Valley, Aoraki/Mount Cook, and the Southern Alps glaciers. The hut overnight option offers a magical sunrise over New Zealand's highest peak.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$4 NZD) into Queenstown town centre. Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a free self-guided walk along the Queenstown lakefront promenade on Lake Wakatipu to get your bearings and enjoy views of the Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Queenstown town centre and explore the night market (held Sundays on Beach Street – free entry, affordable street food stalls from ~$5–10 NZD per dish). Grab a budget-friendly meal from one of the market vendors and soak up the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Queenstown Airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a budget sandwich or pie (~$5–8 NZD) from a bakery or Four Square supermarket near the town centre after check-in
meals.dinner: Queenstown Sunday Night Market on Beach Street – try local street food such as wood-fired pizza, Asian noodles, or loaded fries for ~$8–12 NZD

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Purchase a Bee Card for Orbus buses to save on local transport. Stock up on groceries at Countdown or Pak'nSave supermarket for budget breakfasts and lunches throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown – one of the area's best free hikes. Start early from the trailhead near Queenstown gondola base (walk up through Fernhill to avoid gondola cost). The summit (1,748m) offers panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables. Allow 5–6 hours return for the full summit; the saddle alone is a rewarding 3–4 hour return option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond hike descent or, if back in town by early afternoon, visit the free Queenstown Gardens – a peaceful lakeside park with rose gardens, disc golf (free), and great mountain views. Rest your legs ahead of tomorrow's activities.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Fergburger on Shotover Street – Queenstown's legendary budget-friendly burger joint. Grab a classic burger (~$15–18 NZD) and enjoy it by the lake. Alternatively, cook a simple pasta meal back at the accommodation to save money.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail – sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit bought from the supermarket (~$5 NZD total)
meals.dinner: Fergburger (~$15–18 NZD) or self-catered pasta at accommodation (~$4–6 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking boots and carry plenty of water (2L+) and sunscreen. The Ben Lomond Track is free and one of the best hikes accessible directly from Queenstown. Weather on the South Island can change rapidly – check MetService NZ the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the world-famous Nevis Bungy Jump – the highest bungy in New Zealand at 134m, operated by AJ Hackett. Book in advance online for the best rates (~$275 NZD). Transport from Queenstown to the Nevis Valley site is included in the price. The experience includes the scenic drive into the Nevis Valley, which is right near your accommodation base area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, return to Queenstown and recover with a relaxing walk along the Queenstown Bay beach. Browse the free Kiwi Birdlife Park exterior area or walk the free Queenstown Hill Walkway (1.5 hours return, great panoramic views) as a gentle post-bungy activity.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump! Head to The Pub on Wharf for a budget-friendly meal deal or visit Vudu Larder & Café for affordable shared plates. Alternatively, grab cheap eats from the Queenstown Night Market (check schedule) or cook at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation – toast, eggs, fruit (~$3–5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks and energy bars for the bungy day, or grab a meat pie from a local bakery (~$5–7 NZD)
meals.dinner: The World Bar or a pub meal deal in Queenstown (~$15–20 NZD) or self-catered stir-fry at accommodation (~$5–7 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy is the biggest splurge of the trip. Book well in advance online – AJ Hackett sometimes offers early-bird discounts. Minimum weight 45kg, maximum 127kg. The Nevis Valley location is very close to your accommodation base, making this a logistically easy day. Download your jump video package beforehand if desired (extra cost).

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget Intercity or Naked Bus (~$15–25 NZD booked in advance) from Queenstown to Wanaka (approx. 1 hour). Check in to a Wanaka hostel or leave bags at the bus stop. Begin the free Roys Peak Track – a stunning 16km return hike (5–6 hours) with iconic views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring. Start early to avoid crowds and afternoon heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue or complete the Roys Peak hike descent. The famous 'Instagram ridge' viewpoint is approximately halfway up and worth the effort. Take your time on the descent enjoying the lake and valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka town centre on foot. Visit the free 'That Wanaka Tree' – the iconic lone willow tree growing from Lake Wanaka. Grab dinner at Francesca's Italian Kitchen (budget pasta options ~$18–22 NZD) or pick up groceries from New World Wanaka for a self-catered meal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast before departure from Queenstown
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Roys Peak trail – sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Wanaka town centre – Francesca's Italian or self-catered at hostel (~$5–8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Roys Peak Track is one of New Zealand's most photogenic hikes and completely free. The track can be very busy in summer – start by 7:00am if possible. Carry 2–3L of water as there is no water on the track. Book Wanaka accommodation in advance as it fills quickly in November.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the free Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop Walk near Wanaka (~3 hours, 7km loop). This moderate hike offers stunning aerial views of Lake Wanaka and the surrounding valleys. The track starts a short drive or cycle from Wanaka town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Wanaka and visit the free Puzzling World exterior and sculpture gardens (interior entry ~$16 NZD if budget allows). Alternatively, rent a kayak or paddleboard on Lake Wanaka (~$20–25 NZD per hour) for an afternoon on the water. Explore the Wanaka lakefront and waterfront parks for free.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Wanaka lakefront at sunset – one of the most beautiful free experiences in New Zealand. Grab dinner at Burrito Craft (~$12–15 NZD) or the Wanaka branch of Kai Whakapai café for affordable meals.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel – muesli and yoghurt (~$3–4 NZD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Diamond Lake walk or grab a pie from Wanaka Bakpaka bakery (~$5–7 NZD)
meals.dinner: Burrito Craft or Kai Whakapai in Wanaka (~$12–16 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a great base for two nights. The Diamond Lake walk is less crowded than Roys Peak and equally beautiful. Check if the free Wanaka Running Festival or any community events are on during your visit. Wanaka is slightly more relaxed and budget-friendly than Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Intercity bus or shuttle from Wanaka toward Lake Hawea and then onward to Haast Pass and the West Coast (book in advance, ~$30–40 NZD). En route, stop at the free Blue Pools Walk near Makarora (30-minute return walk through beech forest to stunning turquoise glacier-fed pools with a swing bridge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Franz Josef or Fox Glacier township on the West Coast. Check in to a budget hostel. Take the free self-guided walk to the Fox Glacier terminal face viewpoint (~2 hours return, easy track) for dramatic glacier views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small Fox Glacier township. Cook dinner at the hostel using supermarket supplies (nearest supermarket is in Hokitika – stock up before arriving). Alternatively, grab a budget meal at the Cook Saddle Café & Saloon in Fox Glacier (~$15–20 NZD).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Blue Pools scenic stop or on the bus
meals.dinner: Cook Saddle Café in Fox Glacier (~$15–20 NZD) or self-catered at hostel (~$5–8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~5–6 hours total including stops). The Haast Pass road (SH6) is one of New Zealand's most scenic drives through UNESCO World Heritage rainforest. Book West Coast accommodation well in advance as options are limited. The West Coast has a notoriously wet climate – pack a good rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the free Alex Knob Track near Franz Josef Glacier – a challenging 17km return hike (6–8 hours) through rainforest to an alpine viewpoint with stunning glacier and Tasman Sea views. Alternatively, do the shorter free Sentinel Rock Walk or Roberts Point Track for glacier views without the full commitment.
day_by_day.afternoon: If doing the shorter walks, also explore the free Lake Matheson Walk near Fox Glacier (~1.5 hours, flat loop) – famous for its mirror-like reflections of Mount Cook and Mount Tasman in the lake. This is one of New Zealand's most iconic free photography spots.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fox Glacier or Franz Josef township. Cook a hearty self-catered meal at the hostel to recover from hiking. Relax and plan the next day's activities. Check the weather forecast for the coming days.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the hike – porridge or muesli bars
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch – wraps, energy bars, dried fruit, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hostel – pasta with tomato sauce and vegetables (~$5–7 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The West Coast glaciers are retreating rapidly due to climate change – check DOC (Department of Conservation) website for current track conditions and closures before setting out. Sandflies are notorious on the West Coast – bring strong insect repellent. Lake Matheson is best visited at sunrise or on calm days for the best reflections.

day_by_day.morning: Travel by Intercity bus from the West Coast toward Christchurch via the Arthur's Pass route (alternatively, head south toward Aoraki/Mount Cook). For the Mount Cook route: take a shuttle or bus south toward Twizel (~3–4 hours, ~$30–45 NZD). En route, stop at the free Pukaki Lookout for stunning turquoise lake and Mount Cook views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park village. Check in to YHA Mount Cook (one of the most affordable options in the park, ~$35–50 NZD per night dorm). Begin the free Kea Point Track (2 hours return, easy) for close-up views of the Mueller Glacier and Mount Cook.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the incredible stargazing from Aoraki/Mount Cook – it is an International Dark Sky Reserve, one of the best in the Southern Hemisphere. Join a free self-guided stargazing session or look into the affordable Dark Sky Project tours (~$45 NZD). Cook dinner at the YHA kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at West Coast hostel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus or at the Pukaki Lookout rest stop
meals.dinner: Self-catered at YHA Mount Cook kitchen – rice, lentils, and vegetables (~$6–8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park has very limited and expensive food options – stock up on groceries in Twizel before heading to the park. The YHA Mount Cook has an excellent kitchen. November is a great month for Mount Cook as snow conditions are improving and days are long. The Dark Sky Reserve stargazing is a free highlight not to be missed on a clear night.

day_by_day.morning: Tackle the Mueller Hut Route – the South Island's alternative to the Tongariro Alpine Crossing. This challenging 10km return hike gains 1,000m of elevation through alpine terrain to Mueller Hut (1,800m). Start early (by 7:00am). The views of Mount Cook, the Mueller Glacier, and the surrounding peaks are absolutely spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mueller Hut or begin the descent. The hut itself (bookable through DOC, ~$36 NZD per night) is a great option for an overnight stay if pre-booked. If day hiking, take your time on the descent and enjoy the changing alpine scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mount Cook village. Enjoy a well-earned rest. Cook a hearty self-catered meal at the YHA. Spend the evening stargazing again if skies are clear – this is one of the best dark sky locations in the world.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at YHA before the hike – porridge and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed high-energy trail lunch – cheese wraps, nuts, chocolate, and energy gels
meals.dinner: Self-catered at YHA – hearty pasta bake or soup (~$6–8 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Hut Route is a serious alpine hike requiring good fitness, sturdy boots, and appropriate layering. Check DOC conditions before setting out – snow and ice may be present on upper sections in November. Carry a map, extra layers, rain gear, and plenty of water. This is the highlight hike of the entire trip. Book Mueller Hut in advance via the DOC website if planning an overnight stay.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a rest morning after the Mueller Hut challenge. Take the free, easy Hooker Valley Track (10km return, 3 hours, flat) – one of New Zealand's most accessible and spectacular walks, passing three swing bridges and ending at the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with icebergs and Mount Cook views. Perfect active recovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by shuttle or bus from Mount Cook toward Christchurch (~4 hours via Tekapo, ~$30–45 NZD). Stop at Lake Tekapo – visit the free Church of the Good Shepherd (iconic lakeside stone church), walk the free lupins fields along the lake shore (spectacular in November when lupins bloom in purple and pink), and enjoy the turquoise lake views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Christchurch. Check in to a central hostel (Base Backpackers or Haka Lodge, ~$30–40 NZD dorm). Explore the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens at dusk or walk through the city's vibrant street art precinct.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at YHA Mount Cook – last use of the excellent kitchen
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Tekapo during the scenic stop
meals.dinner: Christchurch – grab budget Thai food or a kebab in the city centre (~$12–16 NZD) or self-catered at hostel

day_by_day.notes: November is the absolute best time to see the lupins at Lake Tekapo – the colourful fields are a stunning free spectacle. Don't rush the Lake Tekapo stop as it is one of the most photographed spots in New Zealand. Christchurch is still rebuilding after the 2011 earthquake and has a fascinating resilient arts and culture scene, much of it free.

day_by_day.morning: Explore free Christchurch attractions: walk through the free Christchurch Botanic Gardens (one of the finest in New Zealand), visit the free Canterbury Museum (natural history, Maori culture, Antarctic exhibits), and walk along the Avon River Precinct through the city's rebuilt heart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free Christchurch Art Gallery (Te Puna o Waiwhetū) self-guided tour – one of New Zealand's premier public art galleries with free admission. Walk through the free Re:START container mall area and explore the city's vibrant street art and murals in the Sydenham and Addington suburbs.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Christchurch Night Market or grab dinner at one of the affordable food trucks in the city centre. The Riverside Market has great budget food options (~$10–15 NZD). Alternatively, cook at the hostel and join fellow travellers in the common area.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Christchurch hostel – toast and fruit
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch from the Riverside Market food hall (~$10–14 NZD) or a supermarket
meals.dinner: Christchurch Riverside Market or food trucks (~$12–16 NZD) or self-catered (~$5–7 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Christchurch is a fascinating city in ongoing regeneration – many of the best experiences are free. The Botanic Gardens and Canterbury Museum are genuine world-class free attractions. The city has excellent cycling infrastructure – many hostels offer free bike hire for guests, making it easy to explore.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Banks Peninsula – catch the Akaroa Shuttle from Christchurch (~$35 NZD return) to the charming French-influenced village of Akaroa, set in a stunning volcanic harbour. Walk the free Akaroa Scenic Reserve track through native bush with harbour views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Akaroa village for free – walk the historic waterfront, visit the free Akaroa Museum, and enjoy the scenic harbour. Optionally, take a budget swim at Akaroa's sheltered beach. Walk the free Giant's House garden exterior or the free Lighthouse Walk (3 hours return) around the harbour headland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Christchurch on the afternoon shuttle. Cook a final self-catered dinner at the hostel or grab affordable fish and chips (~$10–14 NZD) – a classic New Zealand budget meal. Pack bags and prepare for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel before the early shuttle departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in Akaroa or grab a budget sandwich from the Akaroa village bakery (~$7–10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Classic NZ fish and chips from a Christchurch takeaway (~$10–14 NZD) or self-catered at hostel

day_by_day.notes: Akaroa is one of the most charming and unique destinations in the South Island and is completely free to explore. The Akaroa Shuttle must be booked in advance. November weather on Banks Peninsula can be variable – bring a rain layer. Hector's dolphins (world's smallest) are sometimes visible in Akaroa Harbour from the shore for free.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Christchurch. If time allows before departure, take a free walk up the Christchurch Gondola base area or explore the free Hagley Park (New Zealand's largest urban park) surrounding the Botanic Gardens. Visit a local café for a final New Zealand flat white coffee (~$5–6 NZD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: head to Christchurch Airport (Orbus bus Route 29, ~$4 NZD). Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse the airport for any last-minute New Zealand souvenirs within budget (Whittaker's chocolate bars make great affordable gifts, ~$3–5 NZD each).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Christchurch International Airport. Reflect on an incredible 13-day budget adventure through the South Island of New Zealand!

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at hostel or a budget café flat white and muffin in Christchurch city (~$8–10 NZD)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pie at the airport or from a supermarket on the way (~$6–10 NZD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-board the flight

day_by_day.notes: Check out of the hostel by the standard 10:00am time. Store luggage at the hostel or at the airport if your flight is in the evening. Christchurch Airport is approximately 20 minutes from the city centre by bus. This final day is intentionally flexible to accommodate varying flight departure times. Total estimated budget for the 13 days (excluding flights): NZD $1,800–$2,400 covering accommodation in dorms/budget stays, transport, food (mix of self-catered and budget restaurants), the Nevis Bungy (~$275 NZD), and the Mueller Hut DOC fee (~$36 NZD). All other major activities are free hiking and exploration.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport, collect luggage, and transfer to Nevis Valley Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around Queenstown town centre to get your bearings. Browse the lakefront promenade along Lake Wakatipu and soak in the stunning Remarkables mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Queenstown Night Food Tour — explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening food walk through the town centre, sampling local craft beers, artisan cheeses, venison sliders, and New Zealand wines at various stops.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the flight or grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport café upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite at Fergburger (iconic Queenstown institution) — try the classic FergBurger with fries (~NZD 15–18)
meals.dinner: Covered by the Queenstown Night Food Tour — multiple tasting stops included in the experience

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00; nothing is scheduled before arrival. Confirm Night Food Tour booking in advance as it is popular. Transfer from airport to Nevis Valley area takes approximately 30–45 minutes depending on exact accommodation location.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and tackle the Nevis Bungy Jump — leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. The experience includes a scenic gondola-style cable car ride over the gorge. Adrenaline guaranteed. Book the first session of the day for shorter queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and recover with a scenic cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard the TSS Earnslaw steamship. Alternatively, explore Queenstown Gardens with a peaceful walk among rose gardens and century-old trees, or rent a bike along the lakefront trail.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Queenstown's vibrant waterfront. Enjoy a sunset drink at a lakeside bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique stay or at a local café — try The Bespoke Kitchen for avocado toast and flat white (~NZD 18–22)
meals.lunch: Post-bungy celebration lunch at Rata Restaurant's bar menu or Amisfield Bistro for a mid-range NZ cuisine experience (~NZD 25–35)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Botswana Butchery — known for premium NZ lamb and beef in a relaxed upscale setting (~NZD 40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy Jump is operated by AJ Hackett and requires a transfer from Queenstown. Wear comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. Weight limits apply (45–127 kg). Book well in advance as spots fill quickly, especially in summer (November).

day_by_day.morning: Drive or shuttle to Glenorchy (45 minutes from Queenstown) — a charming alpine village at the head of Lake Wakatipu surrounded by dramatic peaks. Take a guided or self-guided walk on the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway, a flat 1-hour loop through wetlands with birdlife and mountain reflections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the start of the Routeburn Track for a day-hike preview. Walk the first section from the Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Flats Hut (approximately 2 hours one way, 5.4 km), passing through ancient beech forest alongside the Routeburn River. Return to the trailhead by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Enjoy a quiet evening exploring the Queenstown night market (held on Saturdays) or browse local boutique shops along the mall.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the accommodation before departing for Glenorchy
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a Queenstown deli — try Patagonia Chocolates or New World supermarket for trail-ready snacks and sandwiches (~NZD 12–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Cow Restaurant — legendary Queenstown pizza and pasta institution in a cosy stone cottage (~NZD 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: Glenorchy road is sealed and scenic — consider stopping at the Glenorchy lookout for photos. The Routeburn day hike section is rated easy-moderate. Wear layers as alpine weather can change quickly even in November.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early for Te Anau (approximately 2 hours drive). Check in to Te Anau accommodation or leave bags at the hotel. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a guided boat tour through an underground cave system filled with thousands of tiny glowworms. Book the morning session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Te Anau lakefront walkway and the DOC visitor centre to learn about Fiordland National Park. Rent a kayak or take a short guided walk on the Kepler Track's first section near the lake outlet — flat, scenic, and perfect for an afternoon stretch.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Te Anau for the night. Enjoy a relaxed dinner overlooking Lake Te Anau.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Nevis Valley boutique stay before departing, or stop at a Queenstown café en route
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Sandfly Café in Te Anau — popular with hikers, great pies and sandwiches (~NZD 14–18)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Pizzeria Paradiso in Te Anau — reliable mid-range Italian with wood-fired pizzas (~NZD 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel day with a 2-hour drive from Queenstown to Te Anau. Book the Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour in advance through Real Journeys. The caves tour takes approximately 2 hours including the boat ride.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau early for Milford Sound (approximately 2 hours drive along the stunning Milford Road). Stop at Mirror Lakes, the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain, and Homer Tunnel for photos along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — paddle a guided sea kayak through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with towering Mitre Peak as your backdrop, then complete a short rainforest hike through ancient podocarp forest. The combo typically runs 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (2 hours). Arrive by early evening, shower, and enjoy a well-earned dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Te Anau before departure — grab a coffee and muffin from a local bakery for the road
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Te Anau supermarket to eat at Milford Sound — there is a café at the visitor terminal but packing saves time and money (~NZD 10–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Miles Better Pies or Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — Redcliff offers a cosy atmosphere with NZ game meats and local produce (~NZD 30–45)

day_by_day.notes: Milford Road can be busy in November (peak season). Depart Te Anau by 7:00–7:30 AM to beat tourist buses. Sandflies are notorious at Milford Sound — bring strong insect repellent. Kayak combo requires moderate fitness and is weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau back toward Queenstown, stopping at Lake Marian for a rewarding half-day hike (approximately 3 hours return, 8 km). The trail climbs steeply through beech forest to a stunning alpine lake nestled below the Darran Mountains — one of Fiordland's hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving back to Queenstown (approximately 1.5 hours from the Lake Marian trailhead). Check back into the Nevis Valley boutique stay. Rest and recover from the active days.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Queenstown. Visit Skyline Queenstown for gondola rides and panoramic views at sunset, or simply walk the lakefront and browse restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Te Anau before departing — The Fat Duck café for eggs and coffee (~NZD 18–22)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Lake Marian — pack supplies from Te Anau before departing
meals.dinner: Dinner at Queenstown's Pier 19 or Rata Restaurant — celebrate the halfway point of your trip with a quality NZ meal (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Marian trail starts from the Hollyford Road turnoff near Milford Road. The initial section is steep and can be muddy — waterproof hiking boots are strongly recommended. The lake itself is breathtaking and worth the effort.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Queenstown. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and explore the Queenstown Arts and Crafts Market (held at Earnslaw Park on Sundays). Browse local artisan stalls featuring NZ jade (pounamu), jewellery, and handmade goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Queenstown Gondola to the top of Bob's Peak for panoramic views over the Remarkables, Lake Wakatipu, and the town. Try the luge rides at the top for a fun, light-hearted activity. Alternatively, visit Arrowtown (20 minutes drive) — a charming gold-rush era village with heritage buildings, autumn-coloured trees, and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a Queenstown food and wine experience. Visit Vudu Café and Larder for a relaxed evening meal, or explore Queenstown's craft beer scene at Altitude Brewing.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Vudu Café and Larder — known for exceptional coffee and brunch dishes (~NZD 20–28)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arrowtown at The Fork and Tap or Provisions of Arrowtown — great burgers and craft beer in a heritage setting (~NZD 22–30)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eichardt's Bar — sophisticated cocktails and shared plates in Queenstown's most iconic boutique hotel bar (~NZD 30–45)

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest and leisure day after five consecutive active days. Use this day to do laundry, recharge devices, review gear, and plan the upcoming Routeburn Track Great Walk multi-day section.

day_by_day.morning: Prepare and pack for the Routeburn Track Great Walk — a 2-day hike starting today. Transfer to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead via shuttle from Queenstown (approximately 1.5 hours). Begin hiking from the Routeburn Shelter, passing through lush beech forest to Routeburn Flats Hut (5.4 km, approximately 2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats Hut up through increasingly dramatic alpine scenery to Routeburn Falls Hut (2.5 km, approximately 1.5 hours). The waterfall views and mountain panoramas are spectacular. Settle into the hut, meet fellow hikers, and explore the immediate surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Routeburn Falls Hut. Enjoy the sunset alpenglow on the surrounding peaks from the hut deck. Prepare and eat a hot hut dinner using the facilities provided.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay or grab supplies from Queenstown supermarket before departing
meals.lunch: Trail lunch eaten at Routeburn Flats — pack sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars, and fruit
meals.dinner: Self-prepared hut dinner — bring dehydrated meals, instant noodles, or pre-cooked food packed from Queenstown

day_by_day.notes: Routeburn Track Great Walk hut passes must be booked in advance through DOC (Department of Conservation) — they sell out months ahead in November. Pack all food, rain gear, warm layers, and first aid. The track is well-marked but weather can change rapidly at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early at Routeburn Falls Hut and continue the Routeburn Track over the famous Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the high point of the track. On a clear day the views stretch across Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Park. Descend to Lake Mackenzie Hut (11.5 km from Falls Hut, approximately 5–6 hours total).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut, set in one of the most beautiful alpine lake settings in New Zealand. Rest, swim in the lake if conditions allow, and explore the immediate surroundings. The reflections of the Darran Mountains in the lake are extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the Lake Mackenzie Hut deck. Socialise with fellow Great Walkers. Prepare dinner and rest well for the final day's hiking.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Routeburn Falls Hut — oats, instant coffee, and packed snacks
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Harris Saddle shelter — energy bars, crackers, cheese, and dried fruit
meals.dinner: Self-prepared hut dinner at Lake Mackenzie — dehydrated meal or packed supplies

day_by_day.notes: The Harris Saddle section can be exposed and windy — full waterproof gear is essential even in November. If weather is severe, DOC rangers may advise waiting at Routeburn Falls Hut. The Conical Hill detour from Harris Saddle adds 1 hour but offers extraordinary 360-degree views — highly recommended on a clear day.

day_by_day.morning: Final section of the Routeburn Track from Lake Mackenzie Hut to The Divide (8.8 km, approximately 3–4 hours). The trail descends through ancient beech forest, crossing streams and passing the beautiful Earland Falls (174m). Arrive at The Divide road end.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the pre-arranged shuttle from The Divide back to Queenstown (approximately 2.5 hours via Te Anau). Return to the Nevis Valley Queenstown Boutique Stay. Shower, do laundry, and rest your legs.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark completing the Routeburn Track Great Walk. Treat yourself to a quality restaurant experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Lake Mackenzie Hut before departing — hot oats and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at The Divide or packed snacks for the shuttle journey
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Rata Restaurant — award-winning NZ cuisine by chef Josh Emmett, featuring local venison, lamb, and seasonal produce (~NZD 45–65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the shuttle from The Divide to Queenstown before starting the track — Tracknet and Info & Track operate this service. The Routeburn Track can be walked in either direction; this itinerary walks it from Routeburn Shelter to The Divide.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 3.5 hours from Queenstown via the Lindis Pass and Lake Pukaki). The drive past the turquoise glacial waters of Lake Pukaki with Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in the distance is one of New Zealand's most iconic road trip moments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Mueller Hut Route — tackle the challenging 10 km return hike in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. The trail climbs steeply from the Hermitage Hotel area via 2,200 steps to Mueller Hut at 1,800m, with jaw-dropping views of the Hooker Valley, Mueller Glacier, and Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724m).
day_by_day.evening: Descend from Mueller Hut and check into accommodation at Mount Cook Village. Enjoy dinner with views of the Southern Alps.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the boutique stay or stop at a café in Cromwell or Twizel en route (~NZD 15–20)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Queenstown or purchase from the Twizel supermarket for the hike
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Old Mountaineers' Café in Mount Cook Village — excellent burgers, craft beer, and mountain atmosphere (~NZD 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: Mueller Hut Route is rated as a challenging day hike — not suitable after heavy rain or snow. The hut at the top can be used for an overnight stay if booked through DOC, but this itinerary treats it as a day hike. November can still see snow at altitude — check conditions with DOC before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn for stargazing at Aoraki/Mount Cook — designated as one of the world's top Dark Sky Reserves. Then take the Hooker Valley Track (10 km return, approximately 3 hours, easy-moderate) — one of New Zealand's best walks, passing swing bridges, glacier lakes with floating icebergs, and culminating at the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with Aoraki towering above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown (approximately 3.5 hours), stopping at Lake Tekapo for a visit to the Church of the Good Shepherd and a walk along the lakeshore. The vivid turquoise water and lupins in bloom (November) create stunning photography opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Queenstown. Final evening in the South Island — enjoy a relaxed dinner and reflect on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Old Mountaineers' Café or pack supplies from the village store
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mackenzie Alpine Café in Lake Tekapo — great cabinet food and coffee with lake views (~NZD 16–22)
meals.dinner: Final dinner in Queenstown at Queenstown Waterfront — try Fishbone Bar and Grill for fresh NZ seafood including green-lipped mussels and blue cod (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is one of New Zealand's most accessible and rewarding walks — suitable for all fitness levels. Lake Tekapo is approximately 1 hour from Mount Cook Village and makes a perfect lunch stop on the return drive. Lupins bloom spectacularly in November around the lake shores.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and a last walk along the Lake Wakatipu waterfront. Visit the Queenstown i-SITE to pick up any last-minute New Zealand souvenirs — pounamu (greenstone), Manuka honey, and Merino wool products make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final activity — consider a scenic flight over the Remarkables and Fiordland, or a relaxed wine tasting at Gibbston Valley Winery (30 minutes from Queenstown), known as the 'Valley of Vines' and New Zealand's highest altitude wine region.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Queenstown Airport for departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring the South Island's most dramatic landscapes, from bungy jumping over the Nevis Gorge to hiking New Zealand's finest Great Walk.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Vudu Café and Larder or Bespoke Kitchen — enjoy one last excellent New Zealand flat white (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Gibbston Valley Winery cellar door, or grab a final Fergburger before heading to the airport (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check departure flight time carefully and allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in. Queenstown Airport is small but can get congested in peak season. Gibbston Valley Winery is open daily and no reservation is needed for cellar door tastings — a perfect, relaxed final afternoon activity.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's most celebrated Great Walks, traversing alpine meadows, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes between Mount Aspiring and Fiordland National Parks. The 32km trail offers stunning views of Lake Harris, the Darran Mountains, and cascading waterfalls. Book a guided day section or multi-day hut experience.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing – South Island Alternative: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Tackle the iconic Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a challenging 10km return hike gaining 1000m elevation. Reward yourself with panoramic views of the Hooker Valley, Aoraki/Mount Cook, and the Southern Alps glaciers. The hut overnight option offers a magical sunrise over New Zealand's highest peak.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with a short rainforest hike along the Milford foreshore track. Paddle beneath towering Mitre Peak, spot fur seals and dolphins, and witness thundering waterfalls up close. This immersive full-day experience connects you with Fiordland's raw wilderness from both land and water.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening food walk through the town centre and waterfront. Sample locally sourced Central Otago pinot noir, South Island lamb sliders, Bluff oysters, and artisan cheeses at five curated stops. Learn about New Zealand's food culture and farm-to-table philosophy from passionate local guides.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer and check-in at the boutique property. Settle in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the immediate grounds and Queenstown town centre to acclimatise. Browse the waterfront promenade along Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle first evening in Queenstown — stroll along the lakefront at dusk with views of the Remarkables mountain range. Early reservation at a top Queenstown restaurant to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport on arrival
meals.lunch: Light arrival meal at Queenstown Airport's premium lounge or a quick stop at Vudu Cafe & Larder for artisan sandwiches and coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Bistro — celebrated Central Otago winery restaurant offering seasonal tasting menus paired with exceptional Pinot Noir; reserve the chef's table experience

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before 13:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from long-haul travel. Confirm boutique stay check-in time in advance and arrange early luggage drop if needed. November is late spring in New Zealand — expect long daylight hours (sunset ~9pm) and mild to warm temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided e-bike tour along the Queenstown Trail network — explore the scenic Arrow River and Lake Hayes loop through Central Otago's stunning spring landscape. A premium guided operator provides top-tier e-bikes, helmets, and a picnic stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arrowtown — a beautifully preserved 19th-century gold-rush village. Explore the Lakes District Museum, browse boutique galleries, and walk the Chinese Settlement heritage trail along the Arrow River.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Night Food Tour — join an intimate guided evening food walk through Queenstown town centre, sampling craft beers, artisan cheeses, local charcuterie, and signature dishes at curated stops. A perfect introduction to the region's culinary identity.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — expect locally sourced eggs, Central Otago stone fruit, house-baked bread, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch provided by the e-bike tour operator — premium charcuterie, local cheeses, sourdough, and Central Otago cherry juice at a scenic lakeside rest stop
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Queenstown Night Food Tour — multiple tasting stops across town; supplement with a nightcap at Bardeaux, Queenstown's acclaimed rooftop cocktail bar

day_by_day.notes: Book the Queenstown Night Food Tour well in advance as group sizes are small and premium slots fill quickly. The e-bike tour is suitable for all fitness levels. Arrowtown is approximately 20 minutes' drive from Queenstown — arrange a private driver or rental.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — the headline adventure experience. Transfer via 4WD to the remote Nevis Valley platform, 134 metres above the Nevis River gorge. New Zealand's highest bungy jump delivers a free-fall of over 8 seconds. Full safety briefing, professional photography and video package included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and decompress with a premium spa session at the Eforea Spa at Hilton Queenstown or the Spa at Millbrook Resort — choose from a deep-tissue massage, alpine botanical wrap, or hydrotherapy circuit to reward the body after the morning's adrenaline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private charter — champagne, canapés, and panoramic views of the Remarkables and Cecil Peak as the golden hour light transforms the lake.

meals.breakfast: Early high-protein breakfast at the boutique stay before transfer — eggs, avocado, smoked salmon, and fresh juice to fuel the bungy experience
meals.lunch: Post-bungy celebratory lunch at Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — Josh Emett's flagship fine-dining spot showcasing New Zealand's finest seasonal produce in an elegant heritage building
meals.dinner: Light grazing dinner aboard the private Lake Wakatipu sunset cruise — curated canapés, charcuterie, and Central Otago sparkling wine; or extend the evening at Botswana Butchery for premium dry-aged New Zealand beef

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Wear comfortable, close-fitting clothing. The 4WD transfer to the platform is part of the experience. Book the spa in advance as post-adventure slots are popular. Private lake charters should be reserved at least 48 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight from Queenstown to the head of the Routeburn Track — a premium way to begin one of New Zealand's Great Walks. The helicopter provides stunning aerial views of Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks before landing at the Routeburn Flats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided hike on the Routeburn Track — traverse ancient beech forests, crystal-clear river flats, and open alpine meadows. Walk from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4km, 2–3 hours), taking in cascading waterfalls and dramatic mountain scenery with a private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Helicopter return to Queenstown from Routeburn Falls. Private transfer back to the boutique stay. Relaxed evening with a long hot shower and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet packed breakfast prepared by the boutique stay — smoked salmon bagels, bliss balls, fresh fruit, and a thermos of quality coffee for the helicopter departure
meals.lunch: Premium guided picnic lunch on the Routeburn Track — your guide carries a curated hamper with local cheeses, cured meats, crackers, dried fruits, and chocolate at a scenic riverside stop
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bunker, Queenstown — intimate, sophisticated restaurant known for its exceptional New Zealand lamb, venison, and locally foraged ingredients; extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: This is a partial day hike on the Routeburn, not the full multi-day Great Walk — designed to experience the best sections in a single premium day. Helicopter access avoids the long road transfer. Wear proper hiking boots and layered clothing. November weather can be changeable at altitude — waterproof jacket essential.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike in the Queenstown Hill Time Walk — a 3-hour return hike rising above the town to 907 metres, offering 360-degree panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. A local naturalist guide shares the ecology and Māori history of the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury wine tasting tour of Central Otago's Gibbston Valley — the 'Valley of Vines' just 30 minutes from Queenstown. Visit two or three premium cellar doors (Peregrine, Amisfield, or Gibbston Valley Winery) with a private sommelier-guided tasting experience including barrel-cave tours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a relaxed evening. Private in-room dining experience at the boutique stay — arrange a private chef to prepare a bespoke three-course dinner using local produce in your suite.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the boutique stay before the morning hike
meals.lunch: Grazing platter and wine pairing at Gibbston Valley Winery's cellar door restaurant — local cheeses, artisan breads, Central Otago charcuterie, and reserve Pinot Noir
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef experience — a bespoke three-course dinner featuring Fiordland crayfish, Canterbury lamb rack, and a Central Otago cherry dessert; paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown Hill hike is moderately challenging — allow 2.5 to 3 hours return. Wear sunscreen and a hat as November sun can be intense at higher elevations. The private chef dinner should be arranged with the boutique stay concierge at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic drive and transfer to Te Anau (approximately 2.5 hours from Queenstown via the Southern Scenic Route) — stop at the Kawarau Gorge and Kingston Flyer viewpoints. Check in at a premium Te Anau lodge as a base for the Milford Sound experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and the shores of Lake Te Anau — New Zealand's second-largest lake. Take a guided walk through the Te Anau Bird Sanctuary to see rare takahē, kiwi, and native bush birds. Optional: Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour (book in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset kayak on Lake Te Anau with a small-group premium operator — paddle along the tranquil lake edge as the Fiordland mountains glow in the evening light. Return for a hearty dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Nevis Valley boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Scenic picnic lunch during the drive — stop at a lakeside viewpoint near Kingston with a premium hamper prepared by the boutique stay
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Ranch Bar & Grill, Te Anau — or arrange a premium lodge dinner featuring Southland blue cod, venison, and local craft beers from Fiordland Brewing Co.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Queenstown to Te Anau is one of the most scenic in New Zealand — allow extra time for photo stops. Arrange accommodation in Te Anau or Milford Sound Lodge in advance; premium options are limited and book out early in the November spring season.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — depart Te Anau early for Milford Sound (1.5-hour scenic drive through the Homer Tunnel). Begin with a guided sea kayak paddle through the iconic fiord, paddling beneath Mitre Peak and the towering 1,200-metre cliffs with cascading waterfalls all around.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Milford Sound combo with a guided rainforest hike along the Foreshore Walk and Bowen Falls Track — explore the ancient podocarp rainforest draped in mosses and ferns, with a guide explaining the unique ecology of Fiordland. Finish with a premium small-boat scenic cruise of the outer sound.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau. Relaxed evening at the lodge — soak in an outdoor hot tub (if available) with views of the mountains. Early night to prepare for the following day.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the lodge before departure — energy bars, fresh fruit, yoghurt parfait, and a quality coffee thermos
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Milford Sound Lodge café or a packed gourmet lunch provided by the kayak tour operator — sandwiches, wraps, local bliss balls, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Te Anau Lodge dining room — fresh Fiordland blue cod, Southland lamb, and local craft ales; or self-catered premium provisions from the Te Anau Countdown with local cheeses and wine on the lodge terrace

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound receives some of the highest rainfall in the world — waterproof gear is essential even in November. Sandflies are notorious at Milford; bring strong insect repellent. The kayak experience requires moderate fitness. Book the kayak and hike combo well in advance as it is one of the most popular premium experiences in Fiordland.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau to Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 3.5–4 hours via State Highway 8 and the stunning Mackenzie Basin). Stop at the Church of the Good Shepherd at Lake Tekapo and soak in the turquoise glacial waters of the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mount Cook Village and check in at The Hermitage Hotel — the iconic luxury lodge with unrivalled views of Aoraki/Mount Cook. Take the Kea Point Track (2-hour return walk) for a front-on view of the Mueller Glacier and the south face of Aoraki.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing experience at the Mount Cook Dark Sky Reserve — the Mackenzie Basin is a UNESCO-designated International Dark Sky Reserve. Join a premium guided telescope session with the Mount Cook Observatory, viewing the Southern Cross, Magellanic Clouds, and Milky Way in extraordinary clarity.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Te Anau lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at Mackenzie Alpine Trust Café in Lake Tekapo — famous salmon bagels, flat whites, and fresh baking with lake views
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Panorama Room at The Hermitage Hotel — fine dining with floor-to-ceiling windows framing Aoraki/Mount Cook; New Zealand rack of lamb, Canterbury salmon, and an extensive South Island wine list

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Te Anau to Mount Cook is long but extraordinarily scenic — allow the full 4 hours with stops. November nights at Mount Cook can be cold (near freezing) — pack warm layers for the stargazing experience. The Hermitage is the only luxury accommodation in the national park; book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Mueller Hut Route — tackle this iconic 10km return hike in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. Begin at the White Horse Hill campsite and ascend steeply through tussock grasslands and scree slopes to Mueller Hut at 1,800 metres. The views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Mueller Glacier, and the Hooker Valley are among the finest in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Mueller Hut back to the valley floor (allow 2–3 hours return from the hut). Stop at the Hooker Valley Track on the way back — a flat, easy 3km walk to the Hooker Lake glacial terminal with floating icebergs and direct views of Aoraki's summit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to The Hermitage for a well-earned recovery. Indulge in the hotel spa facilities — hot pools, sauna, and a therapeutic massage to restore tired muscles after the demanding Mueller Hut ascent.

meals.breakfast: Early high-energy breakfast at The Hermitage before the hike — porridge with manuka honey, eggs, smoked salmon, fresh juice, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch at Mueller Hut — The Hermitage concierge can arrange a luxury trail lunch: venison salami, aged cheddar, sourdough, energy bars, dried apricots, and a thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at The Old Mountaineers Café Bar & Restaurant, Mount Cook Village — relaxed atmosphere, hearty New Zealand cuisine, local craft beer, and a warm fireplace; perfect post-hike reward

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Hut Route is rated as a challenging hike — 1,000 metres of elevation gain over 5km. Proper hiking boots, trekking poles, layered clothing, and sun protection are essential. Check the Department of Conservation (DOC) weather forecast and track conditions the morning of the hike. A guide is recommended for safety on the upper scree sections.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight over the Southern Alps and Aoraki/Mount Cook — a premium 45-minute alpine circuit departing from Mount Cook Airport. Fly over the Tasman Glacier (New Zealand's longest glacier), land on a remote snowfield for a champagne toast, and circle the summit of Aoraki at close range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Mount Cook to Wanaka (approximately 2.5 hours via the Lindis Pass). Arrive in Wanaka and check in at a premium lakeside lodge. Explore the charming town and walk the Wanaka Waterfront Track along the shores of Lake Wanaka.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — the iconic lone willow standing in Lake Wanaka. Enjoy a glass of local wine while watching the alpenglow on Mount Aspiring and the surrounding peaks.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at The Hermitage before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ritual Café, Wanaka — acclaimed for its exceptional brunch and lunch menu; try the eggs benedict with smoked salmon or the house-made granola with Central Otago stone fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — beloved local institution serving handmade pasta, wood-fired dishes, and an excellent Italian and New Zealand wine list in a warm, intimate setting

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight must be booked in advance and is weather-dependent — have a backup plan if conditions are poor. The Lindis Pass drive is spectacular in November with golden tussock landscapes. Wanaka is a quieter, more relaxed alternative to Queenstown with equally stunning scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Guided hike on the Rob Roy Glacier Track in Mount Aspiring National Park — a stunning 10km return day hike through ancient beech forest to a hanging glacier with dramatic ice falls and waterfalls. Depart early from Wanaka (45-minute 4WD transfer to the trailhead at Raspberry Creek).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Wanaka and visit the Wanaka lakefront. Explore Puzzling World for a quirky cultural interlude, or browse the galleries and boutique stores along Ardmore Street. Optional: stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session on Lake Wanaka with a premium hire operator.
day_by_day.evening: Premium wine tasting at Rippon Vineyard — one of New Zealand's most beautiful and biodynamic wineries, set on the shores of Lake Wanaka with Aoraki/Mount Cook visible on clear days. Private after-hours tasting with the winemaker if arranged in advance.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Wanaka lodge before the Rob Roy hike departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the Rob Roy Track — the lodge concierge prepares a premium trail hamper; enjoy it at the glacier viewpoint surrounded by waterfalls
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kika, Wanaka — creative, locally-sourced contemporary cuisine in a stylish setting; celebrated for its seasonal tasting plates, natural wines, and innovative New Zealand flavours

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a 4WD vehicle to reach the trailhead — arrange a guided 4WD tour or hire a suitable vehicle. The track is rated moderate and takes 3–4 hours return. November snowmelt can make the upper sections wet; gaiters and waterproof boots recommended. Rippon Vineyard private tastings must be arranged well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Skydive over Lake Wanaka with Skydive Wanaka — a premium 15,000-foot tandem skydive with views of Lake Wanaka, the Southern Alps, and Mount Aspiring. An exhilarating complement to the Nevis Bungy earlier in the trip, offering a completely different adrenaline perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic float plane flight over the Wanaka and Hawea lakes with Wanaka Flightseeing — a 45-minute premium scenic flight offering unmatched aerial perspectives of the Southern Alps, glacial lakes, and remote valleys of Mount Aspiring National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Wanaka — a celebratory farewell dinner at a premium restaurant. Reflect on the extraordinary experiences of the past 12 days over a long, indulgent meal.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Wanaka lodge
meals.lunch: Post-skydive celebratory lunch at Bistro Gentil, Wanaka — elegant fine dining with lake views, exceptional New Zealand produce, and an extensive wine cellar; one of the best restaurants in the South Island
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The Cardrona Hotel (30 minutes from Wanaka) — a legendary 1863 heritage pub and restaurant offering premium New Zealand lamb, venison, and craft ales in an atmospheric gold-rush era setting

day_by_day.notes: The skydive is weather-dependent and may be rescheduled — build flexibility into the morning. Minimum weight for skydiving is 40kg and maximum is 100kg. The float plane flight is an excellent alternative or addition. November is a busy spring season in Wanaka — book all activities and restaurants well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Wanaka — leisurely breakfast at the lodge, last walk along the Wanaka lakefront, and checkout. Private luxury transfer from Wanaka to Queenstown Airport (approximately 1 hour) for departure flights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Queenstown Airport. If the flight departs in the late afternoon, use the extra time to browse the Queenstown Arts Centre, pick up premium New Zealand souvenirs (Merino wool, Manuka honey, Central Otago wine), or enjoy a final coffee at Vudu Cafe & Larder overlooking the lake.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for Queenstown Airport check-in, especially during the busy November spring season.
